season.evidence: Web: Washington Pass guides give late June to September with snow possible early; only logged summits are Jun and Sep; the one report found had snow trouble in early May and wind in mid-May and succeeded in mid-September. Stored text already puts June as risky.

track.why: Sep 19 2025 report is titled as the north face/ridge, describes 5 roped pitches off the notch side with an exposed undercling and arete near the top, then a scramble to the summit and rappels down the line of ascent; track is a round trip from the SR-20 pullout (59 m from our trailhead pin) to our summit pin (4 m). The only other stored route (Uncle Wehrly's Toupee, 5.10-) is on the Hai Tower subsummit and was not named.

facts.text: Above the lower cracks a wide class 3 ledge leads left to a hole in the wall; the exposed undercling traverse begins just left of that hole.

In mid-September the top pitch was descended on a single-rope rappel, and from the lower ledges a hidden anchor (a nut plus a horn) lies a scramble away, first climber's left then right; the last rappel from the first-pitch ledge drops straight to the ground with no need to traverse.

notes: Only one summited ascent exists; Uncle Wehrly's Toupee (5.10-, Hai Tower) has no track and was not assigned one. The north summit bump was surveyed as higher than the south one; our summit pin matches the track high point within 4 m.
